identity: Front matter plus the opening of a modern (mid-20th-c.) Arabic scholarly monograph on Abu Hanifa. Five distinct layout registers are stacked in one stream: (1) a one-word heading 'iftitah'; (2) the basmala and the whole of Surat al-Fatiha quoted as an epigraph, then Q7:43; (3) a rhymed khutbat al-kitab (ahmaduhu... wa-asta'inuhu... wa-astahdihi... wa-astaghfiruhu..., then wa-usalli wa-usallim 'ala...) lifted from al-Shafi'i's Risala; (4) a three-line footnote apparatus, each line opening with a numeral; (5) the 'muqaddima wa-manhaj' with expository prose plus a six-item numbered plan of the book; then the chapter title 'Asr Abi Hanifa', the sub-heading 'tamhid', and 272 tokens of continuous historical exposition with every paragraph break lost.
law: This is doctrine sections B and L (expository/reference prose): the unit is the printed full stop, and this author's periods run long -- one stretch here (kama taqtadihi bathl al-juhd ... wa-l-athar allati kanat li-hadha al-madhhab, 318-371) is 54 tokens of coordinated NOUNS under a single verb and CANNOT contain a boundary, which calibrates the register at roughly 25-55 tokens per sentence, not 25-45. Default = WELD. I cut only where I can name a typographic reason: (a) every <NL>, free, 100% over 41 docs; (b) a layout slot change where the <NL> was lost -- the list numeral '5' at 429, the chapter title at 485, the sub-heading 'tamhid' at 488; (c) a completed proposition followed by a discourse-restart formula that cannot sit after a comma ('la jarama idhan', 'na'am la-qad'). Connectives earn nothing: wa-, fa-, thumma, kama, li-anna, hayth, ma dama, ba'da an all weld. Comma-lists, appositive stacks, quoted scripture and honorific/numeral groups weld.
reasoning: SCRIPTURE TEST FIRST (doctrine T9). Al-Fatiha at 7-31 is 25 tokens and the temptation is section M (unit = verse). I reject M here for two reasons: this is a quoted epigraph inside a book's opening, not a verse-indexed scripture document; and no aya numerals survive as tokens although numerals DO survive in this document (footnote markers 1/2/3 at 137/144/152, the plan items 1-6, the year 150). With no verse index to attach to, M has nothing to bite on and the Qur'anic text is printed unpunctuated -- so the only mark inside 7-31 is the line end at 32. Zero internal cuts; same for Q7:43 at 33-44. THE KHUTBA (46-90, 45 tokens). Four parallel wa-clauses (ahmaduhu / wa-asta'inuhu / wa-astahdihi / wa-astaghfiruhu). Batch 2 killed parallelism-as-cut (LAW 3, T3 dead) and the Risala khutba is printed with commas throughout and one full stop at 'illa huwa'. Welded entire. Likewise 92-135 (44 tokens): 'wa-usalli wa-usallim 'ala man kana...' followed by a stack of eight adjectival appositives resolving onto the name 'Muhammad 'abduhu wa-rasuluhu' -- LAW 3 apposition-welds, textbook case, one segment. FOOTNOTE LINE 137-142. 'al-zulaf: al-taqaddum wa-l-qurba, wa-azlaftu: qaddamtu' -- two glosses joined by a comma. A2/A4: a prose colon is not a boundary and a comma is never a boundary; the numeral welds to its item exactly as an MCQ option letter does (S3). One segment. 183 (al-zaman), MED. 'Laysa al-tarikhu ... illa san'ata shakhsin aw ashkhasin fi itarin min al-zaman' is a complete 21-token thesis; 'fa-ma min hadathin ... illa' opens its proof. LAW 2 says fa- counts against cutting, but LAW 2's evidence was fa- on syntactically bound clauses (fa-innahu after a purpose clause); here both sides are independent, and a 76-token paragraph with no stop is out of range even for this author. I take it at med. I do NOT cut at 196 or 210: 'wa-ma min dawlatin... wa-ma min nizamin...' are parallel list items closed by the summative 'wa-hakadha ila sa'ir al-mawdu'at' -- the closing 'wa-hakadha' proves it is one enumeration (LAW 3). 240-282 and 284-316 welded entire: trailing li-anna (LAW 4), a three-member 'wa-hiya allati' relative list, ma dama, and 'wa-kana 'amaluhu' with a new subject (LAW 1 dead). 428 (minha), HI -- my most valuable inferred boundary. Items 4 and 5 of the plan share a line because that one <NL> was lost, but the numeral '5' at 429 is a layout slot marker and every sibling item is its own segment. 484 / 487 / 488, HI. Three lost line breaks in a row: the intro's closing prayer ends, the chapter title ''Asr Abi Hanifa' stands alone, and 'tamhid' stands alone -- exactly the shape of 'iftitah' and 'muqaddima wa-manhaj', both confirmed by surviving <NL>. I weld 479: 'wa-llahu yahdi ila sawa'i al-sabil' is wa- + new subject, which LAW 1 (as revised, doc_085c979b884f @489) welds. THE UNBROKEN BODY, 489-760 (272 tokens). No <NL> at all, so I calibrate: at 30-35 tokens the register wants 7-9 boundaries and I place 8. 508 (al-'abbasiyya) MED: a balanced 20-token topic sentence opens the tamhid, and 'wa-bi-dhalika shahida' is a summative resumptive. 553 (ilayhi) MED: shahida / wa-sahaba / wa-ahassa is a three-verb list that must not be broken (so NOT at 536, which would split it), but 'wa-kana li-kulli dhalika atharuhu' is the summative conclusion outside the list -- that is the structurally correct joint. 566 (rayb) HI: 'bi-la rayb' is a clause-final emphatic and 'na'am la-qad ra'a' is a discourse restart. I deliberately do NOT cut after 'na'am' at 567: H3's bare-interjection rule is dialogue-only, and here 'na'am,' is a written concessive particle taking a comma. 601 (al-umawiyyin) LO: the 81-token run 567-647 must contain one stop; the candidates are 580, 587, 601, 611, 623. 587 is impossible (the following 'hadha al-wali alladhi...' is a bare appositive NP that must attach backwards), and 611/623 would fall INSIDE the verb list 'thumma 'asara... wa-akhiran ra'a... wa-sayara...'. That leaves the joint just before that list, i.e. after the al-Hajjaj apposition closes at 601 -- and it yields the contrast 'al-qaswa wa-l-shidda' / 'al-khalifa al-'adil' across the break. Structural, not typographic, hence lo. 647 (al-furs) MED: 'thumma kana an 'asara aydan' is a heavy narrative-restart formula, much stronger than a bare thumma, and it ends the preceding verb list. 687 (al-'alawiyyin) MED: closes a 40-token period; 'thumma kanat khatimatu hayatihi' is the next event. 708 (al-'alawiyyin) HI: 'la jarama idhan an yata'aththara' cannot follow a comma -- it is an evaluative sentence-opener, and 'idhan' closes the whole narrative. The final 709-760 (52 tokens) is one segment despite its length: 'la jarama an [yata'aththara] wa-an [ya'mala] wa-an [takuna]' is three subordinate an-clauses under one matrix, syntactically unsplittable, and 'ba'da an' / relative tails weld (LAW 4). I also refuse a cut at 696-697 ('150 h'): a number plus its era abbreviation is one group (A2).
